name: Matrixyl 3000

lead: Matrixyl 3000 is a branded peptide complex from Sederma that combines palmitoyl tripeptide-1 and palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7. It is used in anti-wrinkle serums for smoother, firmer, thicker-feeling skin and fewer visible wrinkles.

The peptides are proposed to signal skin cells to repair matrix and to reduce inflammation. Its predecessor, Matrixyl (palmitoyl pentapeptide-4), launched in 2000. A 2026 permeation study detected both peptides in layers of the stratum corneum of three volunteers but they appeared to remain between cells. Independent human data on the blend are limited.

paras: It is applied as a daily serum or cream, often in morning and evening routines alongside moisturiser and sunscreen. Wrinkle changes from peptide products are generally assessed over weeks to months.
It is a cosmetic ingredient, and no blend-specific safety data were found in the sources reviewed.

angle.text: Matrixyl 3000 is a two-peptide blend found in many anti-wrinkle serums, promoted for firmer, smoother skin. The peptides are meant to signal collagen repair and calm inflammation, which firms the skin and softens visible wrinkles. A 2026 permeation study found them in the outer skin layers.

lead: Matrixyl 3000 is a branded peptide complex made by Sederma that combines palmitoyl tripeptide-1 and palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7, and is used in anti-wrinkle serums. [1] Its predecessor, Matrixyl (palmitoyl pentapeptide-4), was launched by Sederma in 2000. [2]

Published evidence on the blend itself is limited: a 2026 permeation study reported that both peptides were detected in layers of the stratum corneum of three volunteers but appeared to remain between cells. [1]

paras: The two peptides are lipid-modified fragments proposed to signal skin cells about matrix repair and inflammation. A patent application lists oligopeptide derivatives with acyl groups combined with apple extract for wrinkles, tested in 42 women aged 40 to 70 around the eyes over four weeks. [3]

No independent trial of Matrixyl 3000 itself was found. The permeation study above examined its two peptides in serums on three volunteers. [1] Wikipedia states that efficacy statements on the original Matrixyl are tagged as needing medical citation. [2]
